title: What does the XRPL AllowTrustLineLocking account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of AllowTrustLineLocking and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, AllowTrustLineLocking allows an issuer's trust-line tokens to enter escrow where TokenEscrow is supported. [1]

Unlike clawback permission, this option can be cleared and enabled again. Clearing it blocks new escrows but does not prevent previously created escrows from finishing or canceling. A holder's trust line does not supply the issuer's missing permission. This flag concerns escrow eligibility, not approval to spend every balance held by a buyer. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for AllowTrustLineLocking and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why AllowTrustLineLocking is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
